title: Identification and three-dimensional reconstruction of oxytocin receptor expressing astrocytes in the rat and mouse brain
protocol: Work in a RNase-free environment.
Perfuse the rat or mouse brain to remove blood.
Extract the perfused brain carefully to avoid damage.
Set up perfusion pump.
Attach perfusion tubing and perfusion needle.
Run about 100 mL of tap water or saline through the tubing to remove residue.
Place open end of perfusion tube in beaker filled with cold 4% PFA (on ice).
Open valve on Cole Parmer Masterflex peristaltic perfusion pump.
Adjust to a slow steady drip (30–50 mL/min).
Close valve after adjustment.
Set up surgery site with scissors, forceps, and clamps.
Clean all tools and surfaces using RNAse Zap wipes or equivalent cleaning agent.
Administer anesthetic to the animal (e.g., pentobarbital or isoflurane).
Wait until the animal displays signs of deep anesthesia.
Place the animal on the operating table on its back once it is under anesthesia.
Use both palpebral and paw reflex control to confirm deep anesthesia.
Ensure the animal is unresponsive before proceeding with further steps.
Hold appendages with tape to securely fix the animal.
Pin down the animal using a styrofoam lid and four 18G needles.
Lift the skin and make an incision through the abdomen to verify position.
Cut along the entire length of the diaphragm to expose the chest cavity.
Use sharp scissors to cut through connective tissue at the bottom of the diaphragm.
With large scissors, blunt side down, cut through ribs just left of the rib cage midline.
Make one center or two end horizontal cuts through the rib cage.
Open up the thoracic cavity and clamp it open to expose the heart.
Hold the heart steady with forceps.
Insert about 10–15 mm of a needle directly into the left ventricle protrusion.
For mice, use a smaller gauge needle (21 or 23G) and insert for 5–10 mm.
Perform an incision in the right atrium using sharp scissors.
Set perfusion pump to 10–15 mL/min for rats and 5–6 mL/min for mice.
Start perfusion with 1× PBS at 4°C after making the right atrium cut.
Reposition the needle if fluid is not flowing freely or coming from nostrils/mouth.
Change to 4% paraformaldehyde solution when blood has been cleared (usually after 1–2 minutes).
Avoid air bubbles while transferring tubing from one solution to the other.
Wait 5 s after turning off the pump before switching from PBS to PFA to avoid sucking in air.
Perfusion is almost complete when formalin-induced muscular contractions and lightened color of the liver are observed.
Carefully check for stiffness in the neck of the animal, indicating sufficient perfusion.
Stop the perfusion and decapitate the animal using a guillotine.
Cut along the anterior–posterior axis to remove fur and expose the skull.
Ensure visibility of the spinal cord; if not visible, use a large scissor to remove remaining flesh.
Make two cuts with bone cutter left and right of the spinal cord to bony external auditory canals (ear holes).
Decapitate the animal using a guillotine.
Cut along the anterior–posterior axis to expose the skull.
Ensure visibility of the spinal cord; use scissors if necessary for removal of remaining flesh.
Make two cuts with bone cutter on either side of the spinal cord to ear holes.
Carefully cut along optic tract and remove brain from skull.
Use the bone cutter to make one more vertical cut above the spinal cord.
Use a sturdy plier/forceps to peel off little pieces of the skull until the brain is completely exposed.
Remove or cut the dura mater if necessary to prevent squishing the brain.
Crack the olfactory bone using a sturdy plier.
Flip the brain upside down and use a spatula to carefully expose the optic tract.
Make two more cuts in the top left and right corners with the bone cutter if needed to detach the brain from the skull.
Cut the optic tract using a feather scissor.
Place the brain in a glass vial containing 4% PFA solution and fix for 4 hours at 4°C.
Transfer brains into RNAse-free 30% sucrose (PBS) after postfixation.
Store brains at 4°C until they sink to the bottom of the sealable glass vial, indicating dehydration is complete.
Carefully remove brains from the glass vial once they have sunk to the bottom.
Dry brains using a kim wipe.
Wrap dried brains in aluminum foil.
Store wrapped brains at -80°C for further analysis.
Do not wait longer than 24 hours after brains have sunk before transferring them to the -80°C freezer.
Invert the glass vial carefully if unsure if the brains have fully reached the bottom.
Perform all steps under RNAse free conditions.
Clean all tools, tabletops, brain blocks, and utensils with an RNase removing agent like RNAse Zap.
Remove one brain at a time from the brain jar using tweezers.
Place the brain into a brain matrix or on a flat surface if no brain matrix is available.
Separate the forebrain from the hindbrain using a razor blade.
Store both fore and hindbrains on a piece of foil paper, closing it tightly.
Store immediately in a −80°C freezer or dry ice.
Transfer brains from the -80°C freezer to the cryostat quickly.
Place brains in the cryostat for at least 15-30 min before starting sectioning.
Section brain tissue in a cryostat at 20–25 μm thickness.
Immediately place cross-sections in RNase-free PBS using a brush.
Transfer sections from PBS to a new well using a brush.
Incubate sections in H2O2 (10%) for 10 min at room temperature.
Wash sections 3 times with RNAse-free PBS, each wash lasting 5 minutes.
Mount sections in RNAse-free PBS (pH 7.4) onto SuperFrostTM glass slides by submerging the slides in PBS.
Carefully move the sections to the right position on the slide using a brush.
Pin down the section with the brush while moving the slide out of PBS at the same time.
Draw a circle around the sections with the PAP pen.
Let the slides air dry for 30 minutes.
Dip slides in 100% EtOH (molecular grade).
Let slides dry in the dark overnight or for at least 4 hours.
Remove RNAScope kit from 4°C and leave at room temperature until use.
Place C1 probes in 40°C water bath for 10 min.
Dilute wash buffer (WB) to 1× by mixing 60 ml of concentrated WB with 2940 ml dH2O.
Pre-warm slide box and oven to 40°C for at least 30 min.
Incubate sections in Pretreat 3 (Protease III) for 20 min at room temperature.
Decant Pretreat/Protease 3 solution.
Place slides in a slide rack/wash container filled with dH2O.
Wash slides 2 × in dH2O by moving the slide rack up and down (1 min each).
Remove wash solution from slides one at a time using a kimwipe.
Immediately add 1–3 drops of OTR probe to sections.
Incubate sections at 40°C for 2 h.
Run negative and positive control probes in parallel with experimental slides.
Decant the solution and immediately place it in washing buffer.
Rinse twice for 2 minutes at room temperature, agitating periodically.
Repeat step 29.
Add 1–3 drops of AMP1 to sections and incubate at 40°C for 30 min.
Repeat step 31.
Repeat step 29.
Add 1–3 drops of AMP2 to sections and incubate at 40°C for 30 min.
Repeat step 31.
Repeat step 29.
Add 1–3 drops of AMP3 to sections and incubate at 40°C for 15 min.
Repeat step 31.
Repeat step 29.
Add 1–3 drops of HRP-C1 to sections and incubate at 40°C for 15 min.
Prepare a 1:1000 dilution of Opal/TSA Plus Cy3/5 or far red/cyan colored solution.
Immediately add 1–3 drops of Opal/TSA Plus Cy3/5 (prediluted) to sections and incubate at 40°C for 30 min.
Add 1–3 drops of HRP (horseradish peroxidase) blocker to sections and incubate at 40°C for 15 min.
Perform immunohistochemistry using GFAP and/or glutamine synthetase antibodies.
Prepare 25 μm thick z-stacks at the confocal microscope for OTR-positive astrocytes after RNAScope and IHC.
Adjust laser intensity using the negative control probe to minimize false positive detection.
Incubate brain sections with primary antibodies overnight (at least 12 h) at double the concentration typically used.
Rinse sections twice with dH2O for 2 min at room temperature.
Incubate sections with secondary antibodies (Alexa488/594/643-conjugated, 1:250 or 1:500) for 4 h at room temperature.
Rinse sections twice with dH2O for 2 min at room temperature.
Carefully dry the sections using the edge of a kimwipe.
Apply antifade mounting medium (roughly 60 μL, containing DAPI if needed).
Tilt the slide gently to let excess liquid flow down onto the kimwipe.
Seal the edges using regular clear nail polish to prevent the mounting media from escaping.
Make sure that the nail polish completely dries before starting imaging (at least 24 hours).
Turn on the confocal at least 30 minutes before use and stabilize the laser power.
Put immersion oil on the slide.
Identify the correct brain region using landmarks such as the optic tract or a rat brain atlas.
Verify the correct anatomical location using eyepieces and fluorescent LEDs.
Switch to imaging mode.
Adjust all three confocal channels (red, green, blue) according to specified settings.
Process the negative probe in parallel.
Adjust the 561 nm laser line so that the red channel does not show any signal.
Use the GFAP signal (633 nm laser line, magenta) to set top and bottom borders for z-stack imaging.
Activate z-stack imaging by ticking the respective box on the software interface.
Start imaging by clicking ‘Start experiment’.
Save files in the proprietary Zeiss format (czi).
Filter out debris from the sample.
Cut astrocytes to minimize variables in analysis.
Adjust threshold settings if cell volume averages less than 100 μm3.
Separate software-fused astrocytes manually if surface areas are higher than 20,000 μm2.
Adjust the threshold using the left mouse click by dragging it to the correct position for each z-stack manually.
Check that raw IHC and the three-dimensional surface preview have near-perfect overlap before continuing.
Click on either the blue or green arrow at the bottom right to finish the surface reconstruction.
Carefully check if you are satisfied with the reconstruction by moving around and zooming in and out.
Check if there is sufficient overlap between the fluorescent channel and the surface reconstruction.
If refinement is needed, start over from step 63.
Filter out small debris from reconstructions using the Filter icon.
Select the Volume filter option from the drop-down menu.
Set a threshold to eliminate particles that are too small to be individual astrocytes.
Consistently filter out debris smaller than 100–200 μm³ during post-processing in Imaris.
Click on each astrocyte individually to isolate them for recognition as individual entities by the software.
Use the Cut function to manually cut astrocyte processes at contact points of two different cells.
Cut astrocyte processes perpendicular to the 3D arena ensuring correct position prior to cutting.
Occasionally, use the cut function in Imaris to separate two closely connected astrocytes.
Use shift + left-click in pencil mode to initiate the separation.
A thin blue line will appear indicating where the cut will be made.
Once the cut is made, the astrocytes will be separated into individual entities.
Click on each astrocyte to ensure only one is selected at a time.
Manually delete astrocytes that are too close to the x, y or z plane boundaries.
Left-click on the respective astrocytes and press delete on your keyboard.
Check pre-selected parameters such as surface area, cell volume or filament length on individual astrocytes by clicking on them after selecting Statistics.
Export all collected surface parameters as an Excel file.
View exported files in Excel using respective parameter tabs.
Each row in the Excel file represents an individual astrocyte.
Each column provides information about the respective value and its units for each astrocyte.
Create a New Filaments tab for filament reconstruction.
Place starting points in the center of astrocyte somata.
Adjust the threshold by dragging the yellow line to the left or right as needed.
Rotate the image and zoom in to ensure each astrocyte has exactly one starting point in the center of its soma.
Manually add a starting point if an astrocyte lacks one, by hovering over the appropriate area and shift-left clicking.
Remove a starting point if it is incorrectly placed by hovering over the point and deleting or right-clicking.
Select the correct surface source channel where particles have been filtered out and fused astrocytes manually cut.
Rename the respective channel or pick the masked source channel with the highest number.
Choose the correct surface channel, usually listed at the bottom of the drop-down menu.
Accept automatically calculated starting and seed point values provided by Imaris.
Adjust starting points to be around 25–30 μm for reconstructing astrocyte filaments.
Set seed points to be approximately 1–2 μm for optimal reconstruction.
Place only one starting point in the center of the astrocyte soma.
Ensure seed points overlap with bifurcations of astrocyte processes.
Remove or place starting points manually if necessary using shift left/right click.
Place seed points along the astrocyte filaments based on IHC signal and surface reconstruction using Imaris software.
Adjust the threshold manually for seed point placement to align with filament projections in the image.
Click on the green arrow to finish filament reconstruction.
Export filament data.
Before collecting large data sets using an established Imaris pipeline, review some cellular parameters such as surface area, soma volume, and soma diameter.
Compare these values with literature standards to assess the accuracy of obtained data.
